summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after noticing blood in her nephrostomy tube one week following coil embolization of a failed kidney transplant. She had no pain or fever but presented with an elevated white blood cell count. Imaging showed expected post-embolization changes with scattered echogenic foci suggestive of gas. A sample from the tube grew VRE, but blood cultures were negative and her WBC improved with a single dose of vancomycin. The nephrostomy tube was removed without complication, and she remained stable. Warfarin was restarted, midodrine was added for dialysis-related hypotension, and she completed a short prednisone taper. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue outpatient hemodialysis, monitor the drain site, and follow up with her nephrologist.
